# Endarterectomy

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Surgery > Vascular surgery > Endarterectomy*

[Original Article Link](/library/5l0ixT)

---

## Summary

Endarterectomy is a surgical procedure which involves the removal of part of the inner lining of an <u>artery</u> together with the adherent <u>atherosclerotic plaque</u>. The aim of the procedure is to recanalize the occluded vessel and restore vascular supply to the tissue. Endarterectomy is often done on the carotid <u>artery</u> in patients with significant (≥ 80%) or symptomatic (<u>TIA</u>/<u>stroke</u>) carotid <u>artery</u> obstruction to prevent the development of an <u>ipsilateral</u> <u>stroke</u>. Femoral, aortic, and <u>pulmonary endarterectomy</u> are other frequently performed types of endarterectomy. Complications are rare and include injury to adjacent structures, hemorrhage, postoperative wound infection, and development of <u>false aneurysms</u>.

---

## Indications

* Symptomatic/significant occlusive arterial diseases

* The indications for each type of endarterectomy are

* <u>Carotid endarterectomy</u> (<u>CEA</u>): treatment of choice for patients with significant (> 80%) or <u>symptomatic carotid artery stenosis</u>

* Pulmonary endarterectomy: treatment of choice for chronic thromboembolic <u>pulmonary hypertension</u>

* Aortic endarterectomy 

* Aortoiliac endarterectomy: for aortoiliac <u>peripheral arterial disease</u>

* Transaortic <u>mesenteric</u> endarterectomy: for <u>chronic mesenteric ischemia</u>

* Femoral endarterectomy: for symptomatic lower limb <u>claudication</u> due to <u>femoral artery</u> disease that does not respond to medical management





References:[[1]](/library/zh0rgf)

---

## Technique/steps

* Definition: Surgical recanalization of narrowed/occluded <u>arteries</u> by removing the inner arterial lining (<u>endothelial</u> layer and a layer of <u>tunica media</u>)

* Aim: Removal of the occlusive <u>atherosclerotic plaque</u> together/en masse with a portion of the arterial wall in order to restore blood supply to the tissues

* Procedure

* The <u>artery</u> is exposed, and an arteriotomy is created

* The <u>plaque</u>, along with the adherent <u>endothelium</u> and inner <u>tunica media</u>, is elevated off the deeper <u>tunica media</u> layer and extracted out of the arteriotomy wound

* The arteriotomy wound is closed

* Post-procedure: low-dose <u>aspirin</u> for at least 3 months, often indefinitely





References:[[2]](/library/Z30ZSf)

---

## Complications

* Intraoperative hemorrhage and postoperative <u>hematoma</u>

* Injury to adjacent structures

* During/after <u>carotid endarterectomy</u>: <u>stroke</u>, <u>hypertension</u>, and <u>hypotension</u>

* Wound infection

* <u>False aneurysms</u>




We list the most important complications. The selection is not exhaustive.
